rows.text:
## Proof limits and next gate
This tests acquired significance versus equally used competing episodes, retention
versus access/publication, capacity loss, elapsed time and missing/mismatched cues.
Times400/4000 are idle jumps, not hundreds of intervening cognitive events. Binary
use is not an exact rehearsal count. Admitted/withheld join is not a full same-age,
different-goal meaning experiment; neither false later reports nor changed standing
are new qualified interventions. No acquired identity/self-belief claim. Native
continuation, richer meaning changes, genuine routine consolidation and long-horizon
activity remain separate readiness requirements before declaring the entire old but
defining memory frontier closed. No Brief-clause promotion from this bridge alone.

The successor runtime preserves every native handler and scheduler configuration.
Its only changes are mandatory structural identities, standard publication guard,
and createCanonicalSave using the actual scheduler. Root649 supplies the inherited
analytical anchors. Random-authority IDs and continuing random inputs are empty,
matching this fixed deterministic profile. Save includes full state, allocators,
pending events, committed trace and outputs; inactive/failed runs cannot save.

rows.text:
Restore structurally decodes the closed registered schema universe and Save132,
checks header bounds, recreates the model/run from original inputs and verifies
ModelID/RunID. It replays from S0 to the saved clock, with at most27 actual instants,
and requires complete canonical-save byte equality. Sparse unreachable clocks,
foreign seed/identity, malformed records and any changed save field fail. No saved
state, pending event or transient capability is accepted as authoritative merely
because it decodes. Replay reconstructs pending cross-instant capabilities. The
whole equality check also verifies anchors, version and continuation fields.
